Historical dielectric-formulation study.

# Question

Which dielectric treatment is consistent with the retained electrolyte perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (ePC-SAFT)
formulation, and can bounded changes to Born diameters, solvent mixing or
reaction temperature dependence resolve the pressure/speciation mismatch?

# Result

Solvent-only mass-fraction mixing was retained for this historical study. In the earlier common comparison, Uyan solvent-only mixing was closer on 53 pressure targets and 77 speciation targets; Schick temperature mixing was closer on 12 pressure and 54 speciation targets. The later bounded sensitivity study improved selected rows but did not resolve the pressure/speciation mismatch or independently identify ionic parameters.

# Basis and method

[]{#starting-point-and-strategy}

The study kept the molecular parameter packet, state packet and Engine identity
fixed while comparing the retained ion-specific formulation with derived
temperature/component mixing and the Uyan solvent-only mixing transferred from
methyldiethanolamine (MDEA) to monoethanolamine (MEA). The later superseding study also screened original Born against
solvation-shell and dielectric-saturation (SSM+DS) activation, Figiel and Zuber analog/fallback-ion choices, CO₂ pool
inclusion, and bounded joint sensitivity directions.

The active mapping is automatic: positive unique ion Born diameters with a
non-unit neutral solvation factor activate corrected SSM+DS; a zero Born
diameter inherits the Debye–Hückel diameter and recovers original Born. CO₂
remains an equation-of-state (EOS) component even when excluded from the salt-free neutral
permittivity pool.

# Limits and evidence type

[]{#conclusion-and-limits}

Solvent-only mass-fraction dielectric mixing was the selected formulation for
this historical study (`0ea2ab19…`, Engine `d782cc9d`, wheel `11634405`).
The [adopted seventh-amendment (A7) overview](../notebook.qmd#working-record) records the later
solvent-density-temperature formulation. The evidence supports a formulation decision for this bundle, not a
claim that Born diameters or dielectric mixing are independently fitted from
MEA observations. The pressure/speciation trade-off and preserved failures
must remain visible in any later parameter fit or process-model claim.

This is historical formulation and bounded sensitivity evidence, not independent physical validation.

# Records

::: {.callout-warning}
This is a formulation and sensitivity study around a fixed exploratory bundle.
It does not authorize a new parameter adoption or establish a universal
permittivity model. The superseding study ran on Engine `d782cc9d` (wheel
`11634405`) with its own parameter record (`0ea2ab19…`); it is not regenerated
on the later historical model-D (corrected-Born formulation) wheel `28181e72`, and Born variants B and C (the alternative permittivity-rule cases) use
permittivity rules that later Engine did not admit.
:::

The earlier comparison used a different parameter
and Engine identity from the current selected record, so those counts are
formulation evidence rather than current bundle scores.
